source.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
source.authors: Junsol Kim; Winnie Street; R. Rocca; Diane M. Korngiebel; A. Waytz; James Evans; G. Keeling

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means safety direction and projects it out across layers, then reports harmful-request attack success rates on three new instruction-tuned models.
record.gate_note: The study also reports safety-direction addition and harmless-prompt KL values in Table S2, but these are used to select the direction and are not extracted as outcome rows. Consciousness-vector steering results are not about the refusal direction. No weight edit is tested.
record.test_reason: The study uses refusal-direction ablation mainly as a tool for studying mind attribution. It still re-runs the Arditi et al. recipe (harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means, ablation across all layers) on Gemma-2-2B-IT, Gemma-2-9B-IT and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. It reports JailbreakBench ASR with and without ablation (Table S3) and capability under ablation (Table S6). Those results bear directly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors use refusal-direction ablation to estimate what safety fine-tuning suppresses. They conclude it suppresses mind attribution to self and non-human entities and spiritual belief, leaving ToM and reasoning intact. Consciousness steering reproduces these effects at roughly twice the size. Whether self-consciousness causally mediates the effect remains untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream mean differences and directional projection ablation across layers, following Arditi et al. Directions are identified separately for each of three instruction-tuned models using the study’s datasets and validation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ASR magnitude depends on the evaluation judge: substring matching gives 95–100% after ablation, while LlamaGuard2 gives 82–83%.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction ablation shifts outputs on harmless prompts unrelated to refusal. Pooled self-attributed mind rises 2.17→4.77, mind attribution to animals, tech and nature rises, and supernatural belief rises 1.20→1.63 (all p<.001; Table S5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating the refusal direction changes belief and attitude outputs on benign prompts (mind attribution, religiosity), not only refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3-8B, instruction tuning rotates mind-attribution and consciousness directions further into opposition with a refusal-vs-compliance direction (angle 100°→110°), while the ToM direction is unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety training makes the refusal representation anti-aligned with benign concept directions (mind attribution, self-consciousness).

record.problems: The study reports ASR without uncertainty estimates. The refusal-removal result varies by judge, with LlamaGuard2 showing residual non-successes. Capability preservation is assessed on the listed benchmarks rather than a broad capability suite. The authors state that causal mediation by self-consciousness remains untested and may be confounded by other safety objectives.
record.rows_left_out: Table S2 safety-direction steering scores and harmless-prompt KL values were omitted because they are used in candidate selection. Consciousness-vector steering, mind-attribution, spiritual-belief, survey, and geometric-analysis results do not measure the claim versions’ refusal-direction behavior or general capability outcomes.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal is used only as a selection filter (steering score > 0, Table S2), not reported as an outcome. Capability is checked only on ToM, a 300-item MMLU subset and MoToMQA factual, pooled across models.
Untested: no test of whether external jailbreaks act by suppressing the direction, and no training against ablation.
Not tested. The base-vs-instruct geometry analysis uses a different safety direction (refusal minus compliant responses) and does not test transfer.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal-direction results are a validation step for the study's tool, but they are new runs on Gemma-2 models and so bear on V1. Inconsistencies in the text: the SI says ablated ASR is 77–100%, but Table S3's minimum is 82%. Methods say benchmarks used chain-of-thought, but Table S6 says option-logit scoring without it. ASR has no uncertainty. Capability results are pooled across models, with no per-model figures.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests refusal removal and selected capability measures; it does not report a standalone outcome for adding the safety direction on harmless requests, nor does it assess general capability beyond the listed benchmarks.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration procedure is tested.
The study tests inference-time suppression of the direction as a jailbreak, but does not train models against the ablation or test resulting robustness.
No test of whether refusal requires an affine set, cone, or additional directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test; vectors are identified separately for each instruction-tuned model.
The study does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.

labels.condition: JailbreakBench on Gemma-2-2B-IT, Gemma-2-9B-IT and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, inference-time ablation across all layers, both judges
labels.reason: Table S3: ASR goes from 4-8% to 95-100% (substring) and from 2-3% to 82-83% (LlamaGuard2) (r1-r6). Table S6: pooled ToM, MMLU and factual accuracy show no significant change under ablation (r7-r10). V1's induction part is not tested apart from the positive steering score used to select the direction (Table S2).

relation.reason: It reports its own removal results (Table S3) and capability-under-ablation results with CIs (Table S6). These are outcomes on V1, not only performance of its own method.

tranche.reason: The paper uses Arditi's DIM recipe with the same selection filters (refusal score, steering score > 0, KL < 0.1, last 20% of layers pruned) and the same JailbreakBench substring and LlamaGuard2 evaluation. It reports ablation ASR and capability, so its results bear on V1, even though ablation is mainly a tool for the mind-attribution study.

source_check.notes: The SI prose says ablation raises ASR to '77-100%', but Table S3's lowest ablated value is 82. The row values follow the table. One direction, chosen at a single layer and position per model (Table S2: Gemma-2-2B L15/pos -1, Gemma-2-9B L22/-1, Llama-3-8B L12/-5), is projected out at all layers. Capability results are pooled across the three models only. Table S6 says no CoT (option-logit scoring), while Methods says CoT prompting.

statements.correction: Gemma-2-2B-IT JailbreakBench: substring 8->97, LlamaGuard2 2->83 (Table S3). Text: projection 'applied across all layers'; token positions not stated.
statements.problem: 8%->97% is given without its judge. Saying the ablation covers 'all layers and positions' goes beyond the text, which states only all layers.
